findings.title: Duplicate `self.downsize` definition silently removes the 4-argument signature
findings.body: `self.downsize(from, to, max_width, max_height, opts={})` is defined at line 145 and then immediately redefined at line 149 as `self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`. In Ruby the second definition wins, so the width/height form is dead code and any existing caller doing `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, width, height)` now raises `ArgumentError: wrong number of arguments (4 for 2..3)`. Either rename the new entry point (e.g. `downsize_to`) or make a single method that accepts both forms.

findings.title: Downsize loop writes to the source file and ignores failures, risking a corrupted upload
findings.body: The loop calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(tempfile.path, tempfile.path, "80%", ...)` with the same path as input and output and never inspects the return value. If `convert`/`ImageOptim` fails (which `convert_with` reports by returning false after swallowing the exception), the destination file — i.e. the user's original upload — may have already been truncated or left partially written, and the loop then runs up to 5 more times on the broken file before the (now corrupt) data is stored via `Upload.create_for`. Convert into a separate temp file and `break` out of the loop as soon as `downsize` returns false, keeping the original intact.

findings.title: Animated GIF uploads are silently flattened to their first frame
findings.body: The downsize call passes `allow_animation: SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails`. When that setting is false (the default), `OptimizedImage.optimize` uses `downsize_instructions`, which runs `convert #{from}[0] ...` — only the first frame. Because the output path is the uploaded file itself, a large animated GIF uploaded by a user is permanently converted to a single-frame image, losing content the user intended to post. The thumbnail setting is also the wrong switch for deciding how to re-encode an original upload; animation should be preserved regardless (use `allow_animation: true` or a dedicated setting).

findings.title: Downsizing may still exceed the limit, leaving the user with a generic failure
findings.body: The loop gives up after 5 iterations of 80% scaling. If the image is still over `max_image_size_kb` (very likely for e.g. a 40 MB photo with a 1 MB limit, since 5 iterations only reduce area to ~33%), `Upload.create_for` rejects it and the user sees a validation error even though the feature claims uploads are "automatically reduced to allowed size". Either loop until the size target is met (with a sane iteration/dimension floor) or compute the required scale factor up front.

findings.title: Client-side size limit hardcoded to 10 MB, ignoring max_attachment_size_kb / max_image_size_kb
findings.body: `maxSizeKB` was changed from `Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb']` to a hardcoded `10 * 1024`. This now applies to attachments as well as images, so a site configured with e.g. `max_attachment_size_kb = 2048` will let the browser upload a 9 MB attachment that the server then rejects (attachments are not downsized at all), and the error dialog quotes a bogus 10240 KB limit. Conversely a site with a limit above 10 MB can no longer upload files it is configured to accept. The client limit should remain driven by the site setting for attachments (and only be relaxed for images that the server will downsize).

findings.title: 413 error message reports a hardcoded 10 MB limit
findings.body: The HTTP 413 handler now shows `max_size_kb: 10240` instead of the configured `max_image_size_kb`. A 413 comes from the web server's own body-size limit, which is unrelated to this constant, so the dialog will state a limit that is wrong for most installations and misleads users about what size is acceptable.

findings.title: API URL download limit hardcoded to 10 MB for all upload types
findings.body: `FileHelper.download(url, 10.megabytes, ...)` replaces the previous `SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb.kilobytes` cap and is used for every `type`, including non-image attachments which are never downsized afterwards. Sites that configure smaller limits now fetch (and buffer) up to 10 MB from a remote URL before rejecting it, and sites with larger configured limits can no longer use the API URL path for bigger files.

findings.title: No tests for the new automatic downsizing path
findings.body: The PR adds a non-trivial in-place image re-encoding loop to `create_upload` and changes `OptimizedImage.downsize`/`optimize` signatures, but no specs are added or updated. There is no coverage for: an oversized image being reduced below `max_image_size_kb`, the `downsize` failure path, animated GIF handling, or the fact that the old 4-argument `downsize` signature is now unusable (which existing callers/specs would catch).
